newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone junta spokesman welcomes dialogue.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone junta spokesman welcomes dialogue.

text.p: A spokesman for Sierra Leone's military rulers said on Friday that they were open to negotiations about the return to power of ousted civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.

Colonel Abdul Sesay said the ruling junta welcomed the prospect of a visit by a delegation from Sierra Leone's West African neighbours who called for restoration of Kabbah through dialogue but retained the option of force.

"Who drove Tejan Kabbah away? We did not drive Kabbah away. The AFRC (Armed Forces Revolutionary Council) is open to negotiations about his return as president to Sierra Leone," he told reporters after a meeting of West African foreign ministers in neighbouring Guinea on Thursday and early Friday.

The foreign ministers of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) proposed dialogue and sanctions to persuade leaders of a May 25 coup to restore Kabbah to power and they set up a committee to implement their decisions.

"We are extremely happy with their decision to come to Freetown and examine the situation first hand. We believe that after their visit here they will have a change of mind and economic sanctions or military intervention will not be necessary," Sesay said.

He said this would become apparent when the committee -- Nigeria, Ghana, Guinea, Ivory Coast, the Organisation of African Unity and ECOWAS -- saw the "realities of the peace we have achieved with the RUF (Revolutionary United Front) rebels".
The rebels, who took up arms in 1991, rallied to the coup.
